A1.rationale: New ADR Failure domains and scaling table makes scaling path and failure behaviour explicit per component, and the claims are backed by real Bicep scale rules (min/maxReplicas, KEDA queue triggers), not just prose. Moves from general discussion to documented, partially evidenced scaling.

A2.rationale: ADR Decisions table now names rejected alternatives with reasons (e.g. App Service vs Container Apps, Durable Functions vs scheduled job), moving from default pattern use to deliberate, argued trade-offs.

A3.rationale: ADR adds an explicit threat-model-to-control mapping table and security control list; Bicep modules implement the named controls (Entra-only SQL, disabled local auth on Foundry, private endpoints), so controls are no longer just described but encoded in deployable infrastructure.

A4.rationale: No solution-code artifact exists (file_count 0); nothing is built end to end. Implementation completeness cannot be scored above the floor from planning documents alone.

A5.rationale: Diagnostic settings, metric alerts and a budget resource are now actually configured in Bicep (structured instrumentation), moving beyond qualitative discussion, but the ADR itself states no runtime, load or cost measurement exists yet.

A6.rationale: Foundry now has two named model tiers wired as configuration, but the PRD's evaluation harness still has not been run and no model has been selected on measured criteria.

A7.rationale: The bounded-agent pattern is now enforced at the infrastructure/identity level (agents identity has no DB/blob/Key Vault role, queue-triggered scale to zero), a real guardrail rather than only a design narrative, though no running agent code demonstrates autonomy yet.
